title: 10.104 Determinants of singular bundle metrics
text: Ambient manifolds are connected unless stated otherwise. Fibers need not be connected; the section-envelope arguments treat their connected components separately. Lemma 10.104.1 . EC118288B440 Let $G$ be a holomorphic vector bundle with a singular Hermitian metric which is finite and positive definite almost everywhere. If the logarithm of the squared dual norm of every holomorphic dual section is plurisubharmonic, then the determinant metric has positive curvature. A lower Griffiths bound $-C\omega $ gives determinant curvature at least $-C\operatorname {rk}(G)\omega $. Proof. In a local holomorphic frame write the dual metric matrix as $H^*$. It is locally bounded above: each constant-vector square norm has a plurisubharmonic logarithm, hence is locally bounded above, and polarization bounds every matrix entry. Convolve $H^*$ with a smooth nonnegative radial kernel on a smaller ball. For each holomorphic vector $v(z)$, the logarithm of $v(z)^*H^*_\varepsilon (z)v(z)$ is plurisubharmonic. Indeed for every fixed translation $w$, the translated dual metric has that property for the holomorphic vector $v(z)$, and integrating their exponentials preserves it by the submean inequality and Hölder's inequality. Approximation of the integral by finite positive sums gives the same assertion. The smooth matrices $H^*_\varepsilon $ are positive definite. Their smooth dual metrics therefore have positive Griffiths curvature; taking its trace proves $dd^ c\log \det H^*_\varepsilon \geq 0$. For a radial convolution, the submean monotonicity of $v^*H^*v$, for every constant vector $v$, makes $H^*_\varepsilon $ decrease in the order of Hermitian matrices as $\varepsilon \downarrow 0$. They converge almost everywhere to $H^*$. Hence the logarithmic determinants decrease to $\log \det H^*$ almost everywhere. The latter is finite on a full-measure set, so the decreasing psh limit is not identically $-\infty $ and defines the desired determinant curvature. Local definitions glue by the determinant transition law. For a lower bound, add a local potential of $C\omega $ to each scalar dual logarithmic norm. The determinant weight then changes by rank times that potential, giving the stated bound. $\square$

section: 19.11 Flat twists of adjoint section envelopes
text: Ambient manifolds are connected unless stated otherwise. Fibers need not be connected; the section-envelope arguments treat their connected components separately. Theorem 19.11.1 . 1D4EB7891AC1 Let $Z$ be smooth projective, $(F,h_ F)$ a singular semipositive line bundle with $\mathcal I(h_ F)=\mathcal O_ Z$, and suppose $K_ Z+F$ is pseudo-effective. Let $A$ be ample with a smooth metric, fix $m_0\geq 1$, and put $D=K_ Z+F+A/m_0$. For $\rho \in \operatorname {Pic}^0(Z)$ give $\rho $ a flat metric. In a local frame $e$ of the rational bundle $D$, let \[  B_\rho (x)=\sup _{k,s}\{ |s/e^ k|_\rho ^{2/k}(x): s\in H^0(Z,kD+\rho ),\quad \int _ Z |s|_\rho ^{2/k}h_ Fh_ A^{1/m_0}\leq 1\} .  \] Integers are sufficiently divisible that the bundles exist. The upper semicontinuous regularization of $\log B_\rho $ is independent of $\rho $. It is the regularized envelope allowing all flat twists. The associated extremal singular metric on $D$ is thus independent of the chosen twist. Proof. The envelope is computed separately on each connected component: restriction preserves admissibility, and a section on one component extends by zero to the others. We may therefore assume that $Z$ is connected. Local submean estimates, using upper bounds for the metric weights, bound these logarithmic envelopes above on smaller charts. The bounds are uniform in flat twists: flat unitary frames have constant norm, and their transition functions have modulus one. Since $D$ is big, one divisible multiple has a nonzero section. Starting with this section, the Nadel construction below produces nonzero sections for every target flat twist and every positive multiple of its degree. This also establishes the required nonemptiness; no separate uniform generation theorem is needed. Fix a target twist $\rho _0$ and a nonzero section $s\in H^0(Z,k_0D+\rho )$ normalized to root integral one. The integral is finite since $e^{-\phi _ F}$ is locally integrable. For the Nadel construction choose a positive smooth metric $h_ A'$ on $A$, retaining the prescribed $h_ A$ in the section envelopes. Their weight difference is bounded on compact $Z$. Take $k=\ell k_0$ with $\ell \to \infty $ and all required divisibilities. Write $kD+\rho _0=K_ Z+B_ k$. Choose local holomorphic frames of $K_ Z,F,A$ and unitary flat frames of $\rho ,\rho _0$. If $f_ s$ is the coefficient of $s$, put on $B_ k$ the local metric weight \[  \phi _ F+\phi _{A'}/m_0+\frac{k-1}{k_0}\log |f_ s|^2.  \] These weights have the transition law of $B_ k$, since flat transition factors have modulus one and $B_ k=(k-1)D+F+A/m_0+\rho _0$. Thus they define a metric on the actual line bundle $B_ k$, without choosing a fractional flat line bundle. Its curvature is strictly positive, at least $c_1(A,h_ A')/m_0$. Its multiplier ideal $J_ k$ includes all these weights. It is independent of the flat twist. By theorem 10.102.1 , lemma 10.103.1 , \[  h^0(Z,(kD+\rho _0)\otimes J_ k) =h^0(Z,(kD+\ell \rho )\otimes J_ k)>0.  \] Indeed $s^\ell $ belongs to the right side: after cancellation its weighted square norm is finite and comparable to the normalized integral of $|s|^{2/k_0}h_ Fh_ A^{1/m_0}$. Choose a section $u_ k$ on the left and normalize so that 354F33395764 19.11.2 \begin{equation}  \int _ Z\frac{|u_ k|^2}{|s|^{2(k-1)/k_0}} h_ F(h_ A')^{1/m_0}=1. \end{equation} Flat norms and frame factors are understood in this invariant ratio. Hölder's inequality, the bounded metric difference and the normalization of $s$ give $\int |u_ k|^{2/k}h_ Fh_ A^{1/m_0}\leq C^{1/k}$ for fixed $C$ independent of $k$. Rescale $u_ k$ by the fixed factor $C^{-1/2}$ to make it admissible. This changes its normalized logarithmic weight by $O(1/k)$ and leaves the limits below unchanged. At a generic point of each prime divisor of $s$, the weight of $h_ F$ is bounded above. Integrability in ( 19.11.2 ) therefore forces $\operatorname {ord}u_ k\geq (\ell -1)\operatorname {ord}s$. Normality extends this divisibility across codimension two. Thus \[  u_ k=s^{\ell -1}v_ k,\qquad v_ k\in H^0(Z,k_0D+\rho _0-(\ell -1)\rho ).  \] The weighted norm of $v_ k$ is one for the fixed local weight $w=|s|^{-2(k_0-1)/k_0}h_ F(h_ A')^{1/m_0}$, before this fixed rescaling. Its smooth bundle factor is fixed, and the remaining flat factors are unitary. We check both bounds on its smooth supremum norm, a step needed for the limit. On a finite buffered trivializing cover, $w$ is bounded below by a positive constant. Thus ordinary $L^2$ submean estimates bound $\sup |v_ k|$ above uniformly. For the converse, take coordinate balls $V\Subset U$ from the same fixed buffered cover. The space of sections $J(U)$ of the coherent ideal $J=\mathcal I(w)$ is a closed subspace of $\mathcal O(U)$ with its compact-open Fréchet topology: compact convergence preserves membership in each stalk by Krull closure for analytic modules . Every member is in $L^2(V,w)$: local integrability and a finite cover of $\overline V$ give a finite integral. The inclusion $J(U)\to L^2(V,w)$ has closed graph, because compact convergence and weighted $L^2$ convergence have the same almost-everywhere limit. The Fréchet closed graph theorem therefore bounds its norm by finitely many compact-open seminorms, hence by $C\sup _ K|f|$ for one compact $K\subset U$. All $v_ k$ lie in this same ideal. The fixed smooth bundle factors and unitary flat frames make these bounds independent of their flat twists. Summing over the finite cover gives $1=\| v_ k\| _ w^2\leq C(\sup |v_ k|)^2$. Therefore the smooth supremum is also uniformly bounded below. Choose a fixed smooth metric $h_0$ on $k_0D$. The functions $f_ k=\log |v_ k|_{h_0,\mathrm{flat}}^2$ have a fixed lower curvature bound and uniformly bounded suprema on both sides. Normalized compactness of quasi-plurisubharmonic functions implies $L^1$ precompactness. Consequently $f_ k/k\to 0$ in $L^1$. In local frames, \[  \frac1k\log |u_ k|_{\rho _0}^2 =\frac{\ell -1}{k}\log |s|_\rho ^2+\frac1k\log |v_ k|^2 \longrightarrow \frac1{k_0}\log |s|_\rho ^2 \quad \hbox{in }L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}.  \] Each term is bounded above by the regularized target envelope. The inequality passes to the limit almost everywhere and then everywhere by the canonical plurisubharmonic representatives. Take the supremum over $s,k_0,\rho $ and regularize. This gives the reverse inequality to the evident inclusion of the fixed twist among all twists. Equality follows. $\square$

text: Ambient manifolds are connected unless stated otherwise. Fibers need not be connected; the section-envelope arguments treat their connected components separately. We first give a local estimate whose constant is uniform even when the fibers of a holomorphic map degenerate. Lemma 10.105.1 . 7D9646B80F78 Let $M$ be a relatively closed smooth complex submanifold of $B(a,R)\subset \mathbb C^ N$, of complex dimension $d\geq 1$, with $a\in M$ and no boundary inside the ball. Let $q\geq 0$ be continuous, suppose $q^ k$ is smooth for some integer $k\geq 1$, and assume, away from its zero set, \[  dd^ c\log q\geq -Cdd^ c|z|^2\big |_ M, \qquad C\geq 0.  \] For the induced Euclidean volume and $0<r<R$, \[  q(a)\leq \frac{e^{Cr^2}}{v_{2d}r^{2d}} \int _{M\cap B(a,r)}q\, dV_ M, \qquad v_{2d}=\frac{\pi ^ d}{d!}.  \] The constant does not depend on the geometry of $M$ or on $k$. Proof. First let $w$ be smooth, nonnegative and subharmonic on $M$. Put $n=2d$, $s=|z-a|$ and $I(r)=\int _{M\cap B(a,r)}w\, dV_ M$. Complex submanifolds of Euclidean space are minimal: their coordinate functions are pluriharmonic, hence harmonic for the induced Kähler metric. Thus $\Delta _ Ms^2=2n$ and $|\nabla _ Ms|\leq 1$. This proves the submean inequality for $w$; continuity in the radius removes the regular-value restriction. To apply it to $q$, put $q_\varepsilon =(q^ k+\varepsilon )^{1/k}$. On $q>0$, its logarithm is a convex increasing function of $\log q$ with derivative between zero and one. It therefore has the same lower curvature bound; smoothness extends this bound across the zeros. The function $e^{C|z-a|^2}q_\varepsilon $ is smooth and subharmonic. Divisors mapped into codimension at least two are excluded from this sum. Theorem 10.105.2 . 81245ECD3476 Suppose that for a Kähler form $\omega $ and a holomorphic two-form $\sigma $ on $X$, the class $[\omega +\sigma +\bar\sigma ]$ is rational, and $\sigma |_{X_ y}=0$ on smooth general fibers of $p$. Let $(L,h_ L)$ have semipositive curvature and $\mathcal I(h_ L)=\mathcal O_ X$. If $K_{X_ y}+L|_{X_ y}$ is pseudo-effective outside a proper analytic subset of $Y$, then $K_{X/Y}+L-D(p)$ is pseudo-effective. Proof. Fix a proper analytic subset $W\subset Y$ containing the critical values of $p$ and the exceptional set in the fiberwise pseudo-effectivity hypothesis. Multiplying the rational class by a positive integer and rescaling $\omega ,\sigma $, we can suppose it integral. Over a sufficiently small contractible ball $U\subset Y\setminus W$, Ehresmann's local trivialization identifies the cohomology of $p^{-1}(U)$ with that of a fiber. The class of $\sigma $ restricts to zero there. Thus $[\omega ]$ is integral on $p^{-1}(U)$. Use the restriction of the fixed topological line bundle with this integral class. A unitary connection with curvature $\omega $ defines a holomorphic line bundle $H_ U$ with a smooth metric $h_ U$ of curvature $\omega $: its $(0,2)$ curvature is zero, so its $(0,1)$ part is integrable. Its restriction to each fiber is positive, so lemma 9.71.1 makes the map projective after shrinking $U$. On overlaps these metric bundles differ by a unitary flat bundle. Because their underlying topological bundle is the same, the difference has trivial integral Chern class, also on each fiber. We use the relative Bergman curvature theorem in its precise projective form: for a projective family, a line bundle with singular semipositive metric, and an integer $k$, the $L^{2/k}$ section kernel defines a metric of semipositive curvature on the locus where all fiber sections extend, provided the integrable section space is nonzero somewhere. This is the external variation input of [ Theorem 4.2.2 , PT2014 ] ; its fixed-degree extension is [ Theorem 4.2.7 , PT2014 ] . Both locators refer to arXiv:1409.5504v1 . The section extension hypothesis is stronger than local freeness of the direct image. For each fixed $k$, it holds on a dense analytic open subset $U_ k\subset U$. These subsets may depend on $k$; we do not require a common analytic open subset for all degrees. Over contractible $U$, disconnected fibers give disjoint families of connected components; apply the variation theorem to each of them. Fix $m_0\geq 1$ and put $B=K_{X/Y}+L$. For each sufficiently divisible $k$, the actual twisting line bundle in the variation theorem is \[  L_ k=kL+(k/m_0)H_ U,\qquad h_ k=h_ L^ k h_ U^{k/m_0}.  \] Its curvature is semipositive, and its $k$th-root metric in the fiber integral is exactly $h_ Lh_ U^{1/m_0}$. The coefficient estimate below bounds its local weight divided by $k$, uniformly in $k$, and therefore justifies both this removal and the subsequent regularized supremum over the extended weights. The generic integrability of $h_ L$ follows by Fubini from $\mathcal I(h_ L)=\mathcal O_ X$. Nonzero sections exist on these fibers because a pseudo-effective adjoint plus an ample rational class is big. Kernels with zero generic section space can be omitted. Denote the resulting metric on $B+H_ U/m_0$ by $h_{U,m_0}$. Choose a fixed smooth metric $h_ B$ on $B$, with curvature $\Theta _ B$. The metric ratio defines a scalar function on $p^{-1}(U)$: \[  \psi _ U=\log \frac{h_ Bh_ U^{1/m_0}}{h_{U,m_0}}, \qquad \Theta (h_{U,m_0})=\Theta _ B+\omega /m_0+dd^ c\psi _ U.  \] These functions glue. Intersect the extension loci for the two charts over the countably many degrees, and the full-measure set where the restricted metric is integrable. This intersection has full measure in the base. On any such fiber, replacing one $H_ U$ by another changes the degree-$k$ sections by a topologically trivial flat twist, possibly depending on $k$. Each section for the second choice is therefore admissible for the envelope allowing all flat twists for the first choice, with the same pointwise norm and root integral. By theorem 19.11.1 , this gives one inequality between the two scalar envelopes; interchanging the choices gives the reverse inequality. The prescribed flat metrics occur in both norms, so there is no undetermined additive base function. For disconnected fibers apply this argument on each component: its envelope is unchanged by adjoining the other components, on which the section can be set to zero. The fiberwise regularizations agree by that theorem. A locally upper-bounded plurisubharmonic supremum differs from its upper regularization only on a pluripolar set. Thus the raw suprema agree almost everywhere on each of these fibers, and Fubini gives equality almost everywhere on the total space. After adding the same local potential of $\Theta _ B+\omega /m_0$, their total-space plurisubharmonic representatives agree as well. Hence we have a global function $\psi _{m_0}$ and a positive current \[  T_{m_0}=\Theta _ B+\omega /m_0+dd^ c\psi _{m_0}  \] on $X\setminus p^{-1}(W)$. Fix a total-space coordinate ball $\Omega $, compactly contained in a larger chart with coordinates $z$, mapping into a base chart with coordinates $t$. Write $s=\dim Y$ and $d=\dim X-\dim Y$. For a regular value $y$ and a section $u$ with \[  \int _{X_ y}|u|^{2/k}h_ Lh_ U^{1/m_0}\leq 1,  \] write, in local twisting-bundle frames, \[  u\wedge (p^*dt)^{\otimes k}=F_ u(dz)^{\otimes k}, \qquad q_ u=|F_ u|^{2/k}e^{-\phi _{L,0}-\phi _ U/m_0}.  \] Although the coefficients $F_ u$ use local frames, their metric norm $q_ u$ is a single scalar on $\Omega \cap X_ y$. title: 6.54 Diagonal logarithmic weights
topic: Lelong numbers, multiplier ideals, and regularization
text: Ambient manifolds are connected unless stated otherwise. Fibers need not be connected; the section-envelope arguments treat their connected components separately. Multiplier ideals use the weight $\exp (-\varphi )$. Lemma 6.54.1 . F8F1C7EFDAD8 Let $a_ j>0$, $c\geq 0$, and \[  \varphi =c\log \bigl (|z_1|^{2a_1}+\cdots +|z_ n|^{2a_ n}\bigr ).  \] Its multiplier ideal at the origin is generated by precisely the monomials $z^\beta $, $\beta \in \mathbb N^ n$, for which E7DD351F1AE3 6.54.2 \begin{equation}  \sum _{j=1}^ n\frac{\beta _ j+1}{a_ j}>c. \end{equation} In particular the threshold is strict. Proof. Apply the existing toric monomial integrability criterion on $\mathbb C^ n$ with zero boundary. In its notation the boundary shift is $(1,\ldots ,1)$ and \[  g(x)=\frac c2\log \sum _ j e^{2a_ jx_ j},\qquad (\operatorname {rec}g)(v)=c\max _ j a_ jv_ j.  \] The convention $\varphi =2g(\log |z|)$ is exactly the full metric weight used here. Put $b_ j=(\beta _ j+1)/a_ j>0$ and $t_ j=-a_ jv_ j$ for $v\in -\mathbb R_+^ n$. The canonical strict recession criterion becomes \[  \sum _ j b_ jt_ j>c\min _ jt_ j \quad (t_ j\geq 0,\  t\ne 0).  \] Taking $t=(1,\ldots ,1)$ proves necessity of ( 6.54.2 ). Conversely that threshold implies the criterion when $\min t_ j>0$; if the minimum is zero, positivity of the $b_ j$ proves it directly. This supplies the monomial integrability assertion, including its strict boundary. For a convergent Taylor series $g=\sum _\beta g_\beta z^\beta $, angular orthogonality and Tonelli's theorem identify its weighted square integral with the sum of the nonnegative monomial integrals times $|g_\beta |^2$. Thus every nonzero coefficient of an integrable germ satisfies the threshold. The qualifying exponents form an upward-closed subset of $\mathbb N^ n$. It has finitely many minimal elements: induct on $n$, or apply the ascending chain condition to the associated monomial ideal in the convergent power-series ring. Assign each Taylor term to one of the finitely many minimal monomials dividing it. The resulting quotient series converge on a smaller polydisc, by absolute convergence of the original Taylor series. This proves generation, and the reverse inclusion follows from the already checked integrability of the generators. $\square$

title: 6.56 Singularities along a compact center
topic: Lelong numbers, multiplier ideals, and regularization
text:
Ambient manifolds are connected unless stated otherwise. Fibers need not be connected; the section-envelope arguments treat their connected components separately. The extension below keeps track of a global current and a potential on the complement of the missing set. This permits direct use of Hartogs removal for plurisubharmonic functions, without suppressing the local finite-mass hypothesis in a current-extension theorem. Proposition 6.56.1 . 4E92E37E64AC Let $(X,\omega )$ be compact Kähler, let $C\subset X$ be a compact connected complex submanifold, and let $C_0=C\setminus A$, where $A$ is analytic of complex codimension at least two in $C$. Suppose that $C_0$ is contained in a smooth locally closed complex submanifold $S\subset X$, and fix $y\in C_0$. There are constants $K_1,K_2\geq 0$, depending only on this geometry, such that every $\varphi \in \operatorname {PSH}(X,\omega )$ with a defined analytic-singularity restriction to $S$ satisfies \[  
u (\varphi |_ S,y)\leq K_1
u (\varphi |_ S,C_0)+K_2.  \] The proof also applies whenever the divisorial residual described below has a defined restriction to the exceptional projective bundle. Proof. Replace $S$ by the connected component of $S\setminus A$ containing $C_0$. This leaves the two Lelong numbers unchanged and ensures $S\cap C=C_0$. Write $a=
u (\varphi |_ S,C_0)$. If $C$ is a point, the two numbers are equal. If $\dim C=\dim S$, then $C_0$ is open in $S$ and the restriction to $C$ is a defined $\omega |_ C$-psh function. Its pointwise Lelong numbers have a uniform cohomological mass bound on compact $C$; its generic number is zero. This proves this case. Assume henceforth $\dim C\geq 1$ and $q=\dim S-\dim C\geq 1$. Blow up $C$ in $X$, writing $\pi :\widehat X	o X$ and $D$ for the exceptional divisor. Let $\widehat S$ be the strict transform of $S$, and put \[  E_0=D\cap \widehat S=\mathbb P(N^*_{C_0/S}),\qquad p:E_0	o C_0,\qquad \ell =q-1.  \] The projective convention is the quotient convention for $N^*$, equivalently lines in $N$. The normal subbundle $N_{C_0/S}\subset N_{C/X}|_{C_0}$ extends to a saturated reflexive subsheaf of $N_{C/X}$ on $C$. One may see this in Grassmannian charts: lemma 9.72.1 extends the Plücker ratios across the codimension-two set; their closed graph defines the saturated coherent extension. Resolve the resulting closed projective subspace of $\mathbb P(N^*_{C/X})$. We obtain a compact Kähler manifold $E$, a map $p_ E:E	o C$, and a map $j:E	o \widehat X$ restricting to the inclusion of $E_0$. All these spaces and maps depend only on the original geometry. Choose a Kähler form $\widehat\omega $ on $\widehat X$ and rescale it so that $p_*((\widehat\omega |_{E_0})^\ell )=1$. The fiber integral is constant, not merely normalized at one point. Let \[  T=\pi ^*(\omega +dd^ c\varphi )|_{\widehat S},\qquad G=T-a[E_0].  \] The generic exceptional coefficient is $a$. For analytic singularities this follows by factoring the common lowest normal order in local generators. More generally it is the generic version of corollary 6.53.2 . Divisorial decomposition gives $G\geq 0$. For analytic singularities, after removing the common exceptional factor, not all residual generators vanish identically on $E_0$. Thus $R=G|_{E_0}$ is defined and positive. This is exactly the residual-restriction condition in the last sentence of the statement. Put \[  P_0=p_*(R\wedge \widehat\omega ^\ell ).  \] It is a closed positive $(1,1)$-current on $C_0$. We construct its extension and check its class together. Give $\mathcal O(D)$ a smooth metric, with curvature $	heta _ D$ and canonical section $s_ D$. On $\widehat S$ set \[  B_ a=\pi ^*\omega -a	heta _ D,\qquad \psi =\pi ^*\varphi -a\log |s_ D|^2.  \] Here the norm is that smooth metric. Poincaré–Lelong gives $G=B_ a|_{\widehat S}+dd^ c\psi $, with this sign. E76BA49374E5 Let $X$ be compact Kähler, $C\subset X$ a compact complex submanifold, and $C_0\subset C$ a dense open set with analytic complement of complex codimension at least two. Let $S$ be an irreducible locally closed complex submanifold containing $C_0$, and let $M$ be its analytic Zariski closure in $X$. If $\dim M>\dim S$, then $N^*_{C_0/S}$ is pseudo-effective in the stated approximate sense. Proof. Replace $S$ by $S\setminus (C\setminus C_0)$; its analytic Zariski closure is unchanged, and now $S\cap C=C_0$. Work on one connected component of $C$. The rank-zero case cannot have the stated dimension jump: $S$ then contains an open piece of $C$, so analytic continuation places its irreducible closure in $C$. Use the notation of proposition 6.56.1 : $\pi :\widehat X	o X$ is the blowup of $C$ and $E_0=\widehat S\cap D$. Choose Kähler forms so that \[  [\widehat\omega ]=\pi ^*[\omega ]-\delta [D],\qquad \delta >0.  \] Resolve the strict transform of $M$ by a sequence of smooth-center ambient blowups $p:\widetilde X	o \widehat X$. Its strict transform $\widetilde M$ is smooth and compact Kähler. Choose a Kähler form on $\widetilde X$ whose class is \[  [\widetilde\omega ]=p^*[\widehat\omega ]-\sum _ i b_ i[D_ i], \qquad b_ i>0,  \] where total transforms of exceptional divisors are used. These metric constructions and embedded resolution are the already declared smooth-center resolution input. The map from the strict transform $\widetilde S$ to $\widehat S$ is an isomorphism near a generic point of $E_0$: a proper bimeromorphic map to a smooth space has exceptional image of codimension at least two. Choose one such point $\widetilde y\mapsto \widehat y\mapsto y\in C_0$ once and for all. For the next application replace $\widetilde S$ by its smooth open locus containing $\widetilde y$; this remains Zariski dense in $\widetilde M$. For any $N>0$, proposition 6.55.2 on $\widetilde M$ gives a potential with analytic singularities and restricted Lelong number at least $N$. Reserve a strict part of the background before applying that proposition. The resulting potential has a Hölder exponential and is strictly positive in the remaining Kähler background. The exact submanifold extension theorem for strict positive potentials therefore extends it to $\widetilde X$, preserving its restriction and analytic singularities. This gives \[  \widetilde T\in [\widetilde\omega ],\quad \widetilde T\geq 0, \qquad 
u (\widetilde T|_{\widetilde S},\widetilde y)\geq N.  \] Let $\widehat T=p_*\widetilde T$ and $T=\pi _*\widehat T$. The support theorem and the chosen classes give \[  p^*\widehat T=\widetilde T+\sum _ i b_ i[D_ i], \qquad \pi ^*T=\widehat T+\delta [D].  \] Exceptional divisor classes are independent over pullback classes, as follows successively by restriction to a line in a blowup fiber. Thus their coefficients here are fixed by the displayed classes, independently of $N$. Restricting the first identity near the chosen isomorphic piece gives $
u (\widehat T|_{\widehat S},\widehat y)\geq N$. Put $a=
u (\widehat T|_{\widehat S},E_0)$. The divisorial residual of this restricted current is defined on $E_0$. To check precisely what is needed, work near a generic point where $p|_{\widetilde S}$ is an isomorphism. The first displayed current identity expresses the local restricted potential as an analytic-singularity potential plus fixed multiples of logarithms of holomorphic divisors. Factoring its generic exceptional order leaves a potential not identically $-\infty $ on $E_0$. Positivity extends that restriction over all of connected $E_0$. The second identity then gives the same defined residual for $\pi ^*T|_{\widehat S}$, whose generic coefficient is $a+\delta $. This argument needs this residual condition, rather than an unproved assertion that arbitrary pushdowns preserve analytic singularity type everywhere. Write $\pi _ S:\widehat S	o S$ for the restricted blowup. The second current identity gives directly \[  
u (\widehat T|_{\widehat S},\widehat y)-a =
u (\pi _ S^*(T|_ S),\widehat y)-(a+\delta ) \leq 
u (\pi _ S^*(T|_ S),\widehat y) \leq 2
u (T|_ S,y),  \] where the last inequality is proposition 6.52.1 . This includes the case $\dim S-\dim C=1$, when $\pi _ S$ is the blowup of a Cartier divisor and hence an isomorphism. The compact-center propagation estimate therefore gives \[  N-a\leq 2
u (T|_ S,y) \leq 2K_1(a+\delta )+2K_2.  \] Consequently $a$ tends to infinity with $N$. Subtracting $a[E_0]$ and restricting gives a positive current $R_ a$ on $E_0$. We construct its tautological metric explicitly, since $E_0$ need not be compact. Write $\widehat T=\widehat\omega +dd^ c\widehat\varphi $, using the $dd^ c$ lemma on compact Kähler $\widehat X$, and give $\mathcal O(D)$ a smooth metric $h_ D$ with curvature $	heta _ D$. The smooth pullback of $\widehat\omega $ to the fixed compact model $E$ is bounded by $B\Omega _ E$ for a fixed $B$. Taking $a>B/\varepsilon $ proves the asserted approximate positivity. $\square$

title: 9.74 From local leaves to a meromorphic fibration

section: 9.74 From local leaves to a meromorphic fibration
text: Ambient manifolds are connected unless stated otherwise. Fibers need not be connected; the section-envelope arguments treat their connected components separately. Let $X$ be compact Kähler. The conormal dimension-jump criterion is applied below in $X\times X$, with $C$ the diagonal copy of $X$, $C_0=U$ and $V=\mathcal F^*|_U$. For this section, pseudo-effectivity of a vector bundle $V$ on $C_0$ means the following approximate condition. Fix a smooth compact model $E$ of $\mathbb P(V)$ and a Hermitian form $\Omega _ E$ on it. For every $\varepsilon >0$, the tautological quotient line bundle on $\mathbb P(V)$ has a singular metric of curvature at least $-\varepsilon \Omega _ E$. The constant comparing two fixed smooth metrics is harmless. In the application $V$ extends reflexively across the codimension-two complement of $C_0$. For a saturated involutive sheaf $\mathcal F\subset T_ X$, let $U$ be the open set where both the distribution and its quotient are bundles. Its complement has codimension at least two. Holomorphic Frobenius charts give a smooth germ $S$ of the leaf relation near the diagonal $U\subset X\times X$: two nearby points belong to the same local leaf. Along the diagonal, \[  N_{U/S}\simeq \mathcal F|_ U.  \] Indeed tangent pairs $(v,w)$ in the relation satisfy $w-v\in \mathcal F$, and quotienting by the diagonal tangent identifies this normal quotient with $\mathcal F$. If $\mathcal F^*$ is not pseudo-effective, the preceding theorem forces this germ and its analytic closure to have equal dimension. The final passage is exactly the analytic-graph quotient lemma [ Lemma 7.5 , Ou2025 ] : on a compact Kähler manifold, equality of these dimensions implies that the foliation is induced by a meromorphic map. Its input is the dimension equality, not a second use of the non-pseudo-effective conormal criterion. Here is the cycle construction underlying that lemma. Write $M\subset X\times X$ for the analytic closure and $g=\operatorname {pr}_1|_ M$. Over a dense analytic open set, the general fibers of $g$ form an analytic family of cycles $C_ x$ on $M$. Their proper direct images $(\operatorname {pr}_2)_*C_ x$ are cycles on $X$ whose supports are the corresponding leaf closures. Use these direct images as the leaf parameters: the cycles $C_ x$ on $M$ itself still remember the point $x$ through their first projection. The relevant Barlet component of compact Kähler $X$ is compact. The closure $Y$ of the leaf parameters therefore has a proper universal incidence family. A general parameter has irreducible support tangent to the foliation. Uniqueness of the leaf through a regular point makes the evaluation of the reduced universal incidence family bimeromorphic to $X$. Its other projection gives the required meromorphic map to $Y$. Existence of the analytic fiber-cycle family, its proper direct image, and compactness of the Barlet component are the precise cycle-space inputs retained in the cited lemma. Their foundational proofs remain external; the two projections and the resulting quotient deduction are explicit here. In particular, “induced by a meromorphic map” here asserts compact analytic general fibers. Projectivity of these fibers is not automatic and is proved separately for the positive-slope applications.

title: 10.106 Degrees and maximal slopes
text:
Ambient manifolds are connected unless stated otherwise. Fibers need not be connected; the section-envelope arguments treat their connected components separately. Let $X$ be a compact complex manifold. A degree functional $d$ on torsion-free coherent sheaves is obtained by pairing the first Chern class of the determinant with a fixed real class $\alpha $. We assume $\alpha $ is nonnegative on effective divisors. Thus same-rank inclusions have nondecreasing degree. Put $d(0)=0$ and, for a positive-rank sheaf, set \[  \mu _\alpha (E)= rac{d(E)}{\operatorname {rk}E},\quad \mu _{\alpha ,\max }(E)=\sup _{0
e F\subseteq E}\mu _\alpha (F),\quad \mu _{\alpha ,\min }(E)=\inf _{E	woheadrightarrow Q}\mu _\alpha (Q),  \] where the supremum includes $F=E$, and quotients in the infimum are nonzero and torsion-free. For a Gauduchon form $g$, this specializes to the existing Gauduchon slope : the Bott–Chern first Chern class pairs with the Aeppli class $\alpha =[g^{n-1}]$. In the Kähler case these classes have their usual Hodge cohomology identifications. On a compact Kähler manifold, movable classes are the dual cone of pseudo-effective real $(1,1)$-classes; this agrees with the closure of the Gauduchon test cone through the existing Lamari criterion in dimension at least two. On a compact connected curve, $H^{1,1}(X,\mathbb R)$ is one-dimensional and integration identifies its pseudo-effective cone with the nonnegative ray; the test class $g^0=1$ gives the same dual cone directly. Lemma 10.106.1 . 21D47D6E39D1 Let $E$ be torsion-free. Suppose $m$ is an additive real function on its coherent subsheaves, with $m(0)=0$, nondecreasing on same-rank inclusions. Suppose $m(G)>m(F)$. If $G
ot\subset F$, maximality gives $m(F+G)<m(F)$; degree additivity then yields \[  m(F\cap G)=m(F)+m(G)-m(F+G)>m(G)>m(F)\geq 0.  \] In particular the intersection is nonzero. e 0.  \] Iteration gives a unique finite filtration by saturated subsheaves with semistable successive quotients of strictly decreasing slope. Proof. The preceding lemma for $m=d$ bounds degrees above and therefore bounds slopes above; the rank is between one and $\operatorname {rk}E$. Thus $s=\mu _{\alpha ,\max }(E)$ is finite. Its sum with any other maximizer has that same rank, hence equals it by saturation. This gives the asserted largest $P_ t$. B72C1D61D638 For torsion-free coherent sheaves, \[  \mu _{\alpha ,\min }(E)=-\mu _{\alpha ,\max }(E^*).  \] If $\mu _{\alpha ,\min }(A)>\mu _{\alpha ,\max }(B)$, then $\operatorname {Hom}(A,B)=0$. title: 10.107 Tensor products and involutivity
text: Ambient manifolds are connected unless stated otherwise. Fibers need not be connected; the section-envelope arguments treat their connected components separately. The analytic input for the tensor statement is the following exact semistability theorem: on a compact Kähler manifold, the reflexive tensor product of two sheaves semistable with respect to a movable class is semistable with the sum of their slopes. Its needed Kähler/movable formulation is Ou, [ Lemma 4.4 , Ou2025 ] ; the Gauduchon locally free mechanism is Toma's appendix to [ Proposition 6.1 and Theorem 6.2 , CP11 ] . The Hermite–Einstein existence and polarization-variation steps are retained as deep supporting inputs in the prerequisite register. The following filtration and bracket deductions do not assume an unqualified exterior-power identity. Proposition 10.107.1 . BB9ADDF87BD1 Under that semistability input, \[  \mu _{\alpha ,\max }((E\otimes F)^{**}) =\mu _{\alpha ,\max }(E)+\mu _{\alpha ,\max }(F).  \] The analogous equality holds for minimum slopes. If $E$ is semistable and $1\leq q\leq \operatorname {rk}E$, then $(\Lambda ^ qE)^{**}$ is semistable of slope $q\mu _\alpha (E)$. For a general $E$ one must not replace its largest exterior slope by $q\mu _{\alpha ,\max }(E)$. Proof. Tensor the maximal-slope pieces of $E,F$. The resulting morphism of reflexive tensor products is generically injective, hence injective because its source is torsion-free. Its image in $(E\otimes F)^{**}$ has the sum slope. Saturation cannot decrease that slope, so it gives the lower bound. Tensor the two Harder–Narasimhan filtrations. On the common bundle locus the resulting graded terms are tensor products of semistable factors. Their reflexive extensions are semistable by the input and have slopes at most the asserted sum. The usual image/intersection exact sequences show that a subsheaf of an extension has degree the sum of its filtered degrees. Thus its slope cannot exceed the maximum of the graded slopes. Reflexive extension across codimension two changes no determinant. This proves the upper bound. Duality gives the minimum equality. For semistable $E$, its $q$th tensor power is semistable of slope $q\mu (E)$. In characteristic zero the alternating idempotent $q!^{-1}\sum _{\sigma }\operatorname {sgn}(\sigma )\sigma $ makes $\Lambda ^ qE$ a direct summand on the bundle locus. Its determinant has slope $q\mu (E)$, by counting the occurrences of each basis vector in the exterior basis. The same upper slope bound proves its semistability. For example $E=\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(1) \oplus \mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-1)$ has maximal slope one but $\Lambda ^2E=\mathcal O$ has slope zero. This verifies the need for the qualification. $\square$ Corollary 10.107.2 . 1BF160484066 Let $\mathcal F\subset T_ X$ be a saturated involutive sheaf, and let $\mathcal G$ be its largest maximal-slope subsheaf. If $\mu _\alpha (\mathcal G)>0$, then $\mathcal G$ is saturated in $T_ X$ and involutive, and $\mu _{\alpha ,\min }(\mathcal G)=\mu _\alpha (\mathcal G)>0$. Proof. Both quotients are torsion-free, so saturation is transitive. Semistability gives the asserted equality of minimum slopes. On the bundle locus, the bracket modulo $\mathcal G$ is an $\mathcal O_ X$-linear map \[  \Lambda ^2\mathcal G\longrightarrow \mathcal F/\mathcal G;  \] the derivative terms in the Leibniz rule lie in $\mathcal G$. For rank at least two its source has minimum slope $2\mu (\mathcal G)$ and its target has maximum slope strictly below $\mu (\mathcal G)$. The Hom-vanishing lemma makes the map zero. For rank one the exterior square is zero. Since the target is torsion-free, vanishing on the dense bundle locus is global. $\square$

title: 10.108 Tautological metrics and maximal slopes
text: Ambient manifolds are connected unless stated otherwise. Fibers need not be connected; the section-envelope arguments treat their connected components separately. Let $\mathcal E$ be a reflexive sheaf of rank $r>0$ on compact Kähler $X$ and $X_0$ its locally free locus. Choose a compact smooth model $P$ of $\mathbb P(\mathcal E|_{X_0})$ and a Hermitian form $\Omega _ P$. We call $\mathcal E$ approximately pseudo-effective if for every $\varepsilon >0$ the tautological quotient bundle on this open set has a singular metric of curvature at least $-\varepsilon \Omega _ P$. Changing the smooth metric on this fixed model does not affect the condition, by uniform comparison. Passing to a dominating smooth compact model preserves it by pullback. It does not assert existence of a semipositive limiting metric on this noncompact open set. Lemma 10.108.1 . C0B465266C15 On $\mathbb P^{r-1}$ let $\theta $ be Fubini–Study and let $h$ be a metric on $\mathcal O(1)$ of curvature at least $-\varepsilon C\theta $. If $m\varepsilon C\leq 1$ and $N\geq r+1$, then \[  H^0(\mathbb P^{r-1},K_{\mathbb P^{r-1}}\otimes \mathcal O(m+N)\otimes \mathcal I(h^ m))\ne 0.  \] More generally the same conclusion holds for a smooth auxiliary metric $h_ a$ on $\mathcal O(N)$ whenever $c_1(\mathcal O(m+N),h^ m h_ a)\geq r\theta $. Proof. Endow $\mathcal O(m+N)$ with $h^ m h_{\rm FS}^ N$. Its curvature is at least $(N-1)\theta $. Choose a point $x$ outside the zero set of $\mathcal I(h^ m)$. For $r>1$, the $r-1$ hyperplanes cutting out $x$ give a global logarithmic weight $\eta _ x$ with curvature at least $-(r-1)\theta $ and pole $(r-1)\log |z-x|^2+O(1)$ at $x$. In either formulation, adding $\eta _ x$ leaves strictly positive curvature. Its multiplier ideal equals $\mathcal I(h^ m)$ away from $x$ and is contained in the maximal ideal at $x$, by the pole threshold and upper boundedness of the original weight. The original ideal is $\mathcal O$ near $x$. Nadel vanishing for the new ideal and the quotient exact sequence therefore supply a global section of the original ideal with nonzero value at $x$. This proves the assertion. For $r=1$ the projective fiber is a point and the assertion is immediate. $\square$ Theorem 10.108.2 . 9CD904E0945C If $\mathcal E$ is approximately pseudo-effective, then $\mu _{\alpha ,\max }(\mathcal E)\geq 0$ for every movable class $\alpha $. Equivalently, positive minimum slope of a reflexive sheaf implies that its dual is not approximately pseudo-effective. Proof. Choose a projective modification $f:\widehat X\to X$, obtained by smooth-center blowups, on which $E=f^*\mathcal E/\text{torsion}$ is locally free. Take a common smooth resolution $Q$ of $\mathbb P(E)$ and the chosen model $P$, projective over $\widehat X$, with $q:Q\to \mathbb P(E)$ and $\pi :Q\to \widehat X$. All maps are isomorphisms on the original projective bundle over $X_0$. We do not require a morphism from $\mathbb P(E)$ itself to an arbitrary chosen resolution. Fix a relatively ample line bundle $A$ on $Q$. A smooth metric on it has curvature $\theta _ A$ with $\theta _ A+C_0\pi ^*\widehat\omega >0$. Increasing its fixed power if necessary, its vertical curvature dominates $(r+1)$ times the Fubini–Study form pulled back from $\mathbb P(E)$. Indeed this comparison holds uniformly on compact $Q$ after a base form is added. The pullback of the error form $\Omega _ P$ is bounded by a fixed multiple of $\theta _ A+C_0\pi ^*\widehat\omega $. For each $m$, take $\varepsilon _ m$ so small that its product with $m$ and this bound leaves both a positive vertical margin and a base lower bound $-C_1\pi ^*\widehat\omega $, with $C_1$ independent of $m$. Then $h_{\varepsilon _ m}^ m h_ A$ on $q^*\mathcal O(m)\otimes A$ has that lower bound; its ideal is $\mathcal I(h_{\varepsilon _ m}^ m)$. On the open bundle locus write $A=\mathcal O(N)\otimes \pi ^*B$ with fixed $N\geq r+1$. Here $B$ extends to a line bundle on $\widehat X$: first $(q_*A)^{**}$ is a line bundle on the smooth $\mathbb P(E)$, and its projective-bundle Picard decomposition has this form; the difference upstairs is supported on the exceptional divisors. On $f^{-1}(X_0)$ consider \[  G_ m=\pi _*\bigl (K_{Q/\widehat X}\otimes q^*\mathcal O(m)\otimes A\otimes \mathcal I(h_{\varepsilon _ m}^ m)\bigr ).  \] The fiber lemma makes this sheaf nonzero. More precisely choose a general base point where the multiplier ideal restricts to the fiber ideal, outside the exceptional set furnished by Fubini and the restriction/extension theorem for multiplier ideals. Fiberwise $L^2$ extension then identifies the nonzero fiber space with locally extendable sections. These are the generic base-change and extension conditions used here. The singular $L^2$ direct-image theorem, applied after a local base twist with curvature $C_1\widehat\omega $, gives a metric on $G_ m$ with Griffiths curvature at least $-C_1\widehat\omega \otimes \operatorname {Id}$. For this multiplier-ideal direct image the exact external input is [ Theorem 21.1 , HPS2017 ] , in arXiv:1611.08768v2 ; determinant positivity follows from lemma 10.104.1 . The generic-isomorphism restriction of the earlier Păun–Takayama formulation is not assumed automatically. In particular, \[  c_1(\det G_ m,\det h_ m)\geq -C_1\operatorname {rk}(G_ m)\widehat\omega .  \] We now descend the direct image and its determinant metric. In the quotient convention, $K_{\mathbb P(E)/\widehat X}=\mathcal O(-r)\otimes \pi ^*\det E$. The fixed $B$ descends, modulo exceptional divisors, to a line bundle $M$ on smooth $X$, by the same reflexive-pushforward argument. Thus $G_ m$ is a subsheaf of $M\otimes \det \mathcal E\otimes \operatorname {Sym}^{m+N-r}\mathcal E$ on $X_0$. Saturate it there. Its Grassmannian map extends meromorphically across $X\setminus X_0$ by lemma 9.72.1 , giving a coherent saturated subsheaf $\overline G_ m$ of the reflexive ambient sheaf on $X$. Saturation changes its determinant by an effective divisor, so the determinant metric's lower curvature bound persists after adding that divisor metric. The error can be transferred to $X$ using a fixed scalar weight. The existing exceptional correction lemma gives an effective rational exceptional divisor $D$ and a Kähler form $\gamma $ in $f^*[\omega _ X]-[D]$. Choose component metrics, with combined curvature $\Theta _ D$ and logarithmic section norm $L_ D$, so that $dd^ cL_ D=[D]-\Theta _ D$. The $dd^ c$-lemma gives a smooth $u$ with $\gamma =f^*\omega _ X-\Theta _ D+dd^ cu$. Hence \[  f^*\omega _ X+dd^ c(L_ D+u)=\gamma +[D]\geq 0.  \] By the existing plurisubharmonic descent theorem , $L_ D+u=f^*\rho $ for a global $\omega _ X$-psh function $\rho $. It is smooth off the exceptional image, where $f^*(\omega _ X+dd^ c\rho )=\gamma $. Uniform comparison of the two fixed Kähler forms on compact $\widehat X$ yields $C_2$ with \[  \widehat\omega \leq C_2 f^*(\omega _ X+dd^ c\rho )  \] off that image. All these choices are fixed before $m$ varies. Put $c=C_1C_2\operatorname {rk}(G_ m)$ and add $c\rho $ to the determinant weight on $X_0$. Its curvature is then at least $-c\omega _ X$. After a smooth local potential is added, it is plurisubharmonic. Codimension-two removal extends it to a metric on $\det \overline G_ m$. title: Lemma 10.108.1
text: Ambient manifolds are connected unless stated otherwise. Fibers need not be connected; the section-envelope arguments treat their connected components separately. Lemma 10.108.1 . C0B465266C15 On $\mathbb P^{r-1}$ let $\theta $ be Fubini–Study and let $h$ be a metric on $\mathcal O(1)$ of curvature at least $-\varepsilon C\theta $. If $m\varepsilon C\leq 1$ and $N\geq r+1$, then \[  H^0(\mathbb P^{r-1},K_{\mathbb P^{r-1}}\otimes \mathcal O(m+N)\otimes \mathcal I(h^ m))\ne 0.  \] More generally the same conclusion holds for a smooth auxiliary metric $h_ a$ on $\mathcal O(N)$ whenever $c_1(\mathcal O(m+N),h^ m h_ a)\geq r\theta $. Proof. Endow $\mathcal O(m+N)$ with $h^ m h_{\rm FS}^ N$. Its curvature is at least $(N-1)\theta $. Choose a point $x$ outside the zero set of $\mathcal I(h^ m)$. For $r>1$, the $r-1$ hyperplanes cutting out $x$ give a global logarithmic weight $\eta _ x$ with curvature at least $-(r-1)\theta $ and pole $(r-1)\log |z-x|^2+O(1)$ at $x$. The original ideal is $\mathcal O$ near $x$. Nadel vanishing for the new ideal and the quotient exact sequence therefore supply a global section of the original ideal with nonzero value at $x$. title: Theorem 10.108.2
text: Ambient manifolds are connected unless stated otherwise. Fibers need not be connected; the section-envelope arguments treat their connected components separately. Let $\mathcal E$ be a reflexive sheaf of rank $r>0$ on compact Kähler $X$ and $X_0$ its locally free locus. Choose a compact smooth model $P$ of $\mathbb P(\mathcal E|_{X_0})$ and a Hermitian form $\Omega _ P$. We call $\mathcal E$ approximately pseudo-effective if for every $\varepsilon >0$ the tautological quotient bundle on this open set has a singular metric of curvature at least $-\varepsilon \Omega _ P$. Changing the smooth metric on this fixed model does not affect the condition, by uniform comparison. Passing to a dominating smooth compact model preserves it by pullback. It does not assert existence of a semipositive limiting metric on this noncompact open set. Theorem 10.108.2 . 9CD904E0945C If $\mathcal E$ is approximately pseudo-effective, then $\mu _{\alpha ,\max }(\mathcal E)\geq 0$ for every movable class $\alpha $. Equivalently, positive minimum slope of a reflexive sheaf implies that its dual is not approximately pseudo-effective. Proof. Choose a projective modification $f:\widehat X\to X$, obtained by smooth-center blowups, on which $E=f^*\mathcal E/\text{torsion}$ is locally free. Take a common smooth resolution $Q$ of $\mathbb P(E)$ and the chosen model $P$, projective over $\widehat X$, with $q:Q\to \mathbb P(E)$ and $\pi :Q\to \widehat X$. All maps are isomorphisms on the original projective bundle over $X_0$. We do not require a morphism from $\mathbb P(E)$ itself to an arbitrary chosen resolution. Fix a relatively ample line bundle $A$ on $Q$. A smooth metric on it has curvature $\theta _ A$ with $\theta _ A+C_0\pi ^*\widehat\omega >0$. Increasing its fixed power if necessary, its vertical curvature dominates $(r+1)$ times the Fubini–Study form pulled back from $\mathbb P(E)$. Indeed this comparison holds uniformly on compact $Q$ after a base form is added. The pullback of the error form $\Omega _ P$ is bounded by a fixed multiple of $\theta _ A+C_0\pi ^*\widehat\omega $. For each $m$, take $\varepsilon _ m$ so small that its product with $m$ and this bound leaves both a positive vertical margin and a base lower bound $-C_1\pi ^*\widehat\omega $, with $C_1$ independent of $m$. Then $h_{\varepsilon _ m}^ m h_ A$ on $q^*\mathcal O(m)\otimes A$ has that lower bound; its ideal is $\mathcal I(h_{\varepsilon _ m}^ m)$. On the open bundle locus write $A=\mathcal O(N)\otimes \pi ^*B$ with fixed $N\geq r+1$. Here $B$ extends to a line bundle on $\widehat X$: first $(q_*A)^{**}$ is a line bundle on the smooth $\mathbb P(E)$, and its projective-bundle Picard decomposition has this form; the difference upstairs is supported on the exceptional divisors. On $f^{-1}(X_0)$ consider \[  G_ m=\pi _*\bigl (K_{Q/\widehat X}\otimes q^*\mathcal O(m)\otimes A\otimes \mathcal I(h_{\varepsilon _ m}^ m)\bigr ).  \] The fiber lemma makes this sheaf nonzero. More precisely choose a general base point where the multiplier ideal restricts to the fiber ideal, outside the exceptional set furnished by Fubini and the restriction/extension theorem for multiplier ideals. Fiberwise $L^2$ extension then identifies the nonzero fiber space with locally extendable sections. These are the generic base-change and extension conditions used here. The singular $L^2$ direct-image theorem, applied after a local base twist with curvature $C_1\widehat\omega $, gives a metric on $G_ m$ with Griffiths curvature at least $-C_1\widehat\omega \otimes \operatorname {Id}$. For this multiplier-ideal direct image the exact external input is [ Theorem 21.1 , HPS2017 ] , in arXiv:1611.08768v2 ; determinant positivity follows from lemma 10.104.1 . The generic-isomorphism restriction of the earlier Păun–Takayama formulation is not assumed automatically. In particular, \[  c_1(\det G_ m,\det h_ m)\geq -C_1\operatorname {rk}(G_ m)\widehat\omega .  \] We now descend the direct image and its determinant metric. In the quotient convention, $K_{\mathbb P(E)/\widehat X}=\mathcal O(-r)\otimes \pi ^*\det E$. The fixed $B$ descends, modulo exceptional divisors, to a line bundle $M$ on smooth $X$, by the same reflexive-pushforward argument. Thus $G_ m$ is a subsheaf of $M\otimes \det \mathcal E\otimes \operatorname {Sym}^{m+N-r}\mathcal E$ on $X_0$. Saturate it there. Its Grassmannian map extends meromorphically across $X\setminus X_0$ by lemma 9.72.1 , giving a coherent saturated subsheaf $\overline G_ m$ of the reflexive ambient sheaf on $X$. Saturation changes its determinant by an effective divisor, so the determinant metric's lower curvature bound persists after adding that divisor metric. The error can be transferred to $X$ using a fixed scalar weight. The existing exceptional correction lemma gives an effective rational exceptional divisor $D$ and a Kähler form $\gamma $ in $f^*[\omega _ X]-[D]$. Choose component metrics, with combined curvature $\Theta _ D$ and logarithmic section norm $L_ D$, so that $dd^ cL_ D=[D]-\Theta _ D$. The $dd^ c$-lemma gives a smooth $u$ with $\gamma =f^*\omega _ X-\Theta _ D+dd^ cu$. Hence \[  f^*\omega _ X+dd^ c(L_ D+u)=\gamma +[D]\geq 0.  \] By the existing plurisubharmonic descent theorem , $L_ D+u=f^*\rho $ for a global $\omega _ X$-psh function $\rho $. It is smooth off the exceptional image, where $f^*(\omega _ X+dd^ c\rho )=\gamma $. Uniform comparison of the two fixed Kähler forms on compact $\widehat X$ yields $C_2$ with \[  \widehat\omega \leq C_2 f^*(\omega _ X+dd^ c\rho )  \] off that image. title: 9.75 Holomorphic forms and positive foliations
text: Ambient manifolds are connected unless stated otherwise. Fibers need not be connected; the section-envelope arguments treat their connected components separately. Lemma 9.75.1 . 597700D273A6 Every compact Kähler manifold $Z$ admits a Kähler form $a$ and a holomorphic two-form $\tau $ with $[a+\tau +\bar\tau ]\in H^2(Z,\mathbb Q)$. Proof. The rational lattice comparison makes rational classes dense in real degree-two cohomology. Choose one sufficiently close to a fixed Kähler class. Its Hodge $(1,1)$ component is still Kähler, since the Kähler cone is open. Represent that component by $a$ and the $(2,0)$ component by its holomorphic representative $\tau $. The $(0,2)$ component is the complex conjugate. The Kähler Hodge decomposition proves the claim. $\square$ Lemma 9.75.2 . B52F345AB247 Let $\mathcal F\subset T_ X$ be saturated and have $\mu _{\alpha ,\min }(\mathcal F)>0$ on compact Kähler $X$. Every holomorphic two-form on $X$ restricts to zero on $\Lambda ^2\mathcal F$. The assertion remains true on a smooth modification, for the induced foliation and pulled-back movable class. Proof. The reflexive exterior square is a quotient of the reflexive tensor square. Its minimum slope is therefore at least $2\mu _{\alpha ,\min }(\mathcal F)>0$ by proposition 10.107.1 . A two-form gives a morphism from this exterior square to $\mathcal O_ X$; Hom vanishing makes it zero. In rank one there is no exterior square. For a modification $\pi $, define the pulled-back movable functional by pairing with the pushforward of divisor classes. It is nonnegative on positive classes and annihilates exceptional divisors. Determinants of induced subsheaves and quotients change only by exceptional divisors. Pushing their generic maps down proves preservation of the extremal slopes. Also holomorphic two-forms on the modification descend off the exceptional image and extend coefficientwise across its codimension-two complement by Hartogs. This proves the last assertion without any new choice of a particular two-form. $\square$ Theorem 9.75.3 . CDF6A16B105C Let $X$ be compact Kähler and let $\mathcal F\subset T_ X$ be a nonzero saturated involutive sheaf. If $\mu _{\alpha ,\min }(\mathcal F)>0$ for a movable class, it is induced by a meromorphic fibration whose smooth general fibers are rationally connected. Proof. By the tautological slope criterion, $\mathcal F^*$ is not pseudo-effective. The conormal criterion and the cycle-space leaf quotient give a meromorphic fibration inducing $\mathcal F$. Its quotient has a compact Kähler model by the class-C image theorem, as in [ Lemma 8.2 , Ou2025 ] . We first specify the models needed below. For a holomorphic fibration $f:U\to V$ of compact Kähler manifolds, the geometric flattening theorem [ Theorem 1.7 , Campana2004 ] gives a meromorphic fiber-cycle map $V\dashrightarrow \mathcal C(U)$. Resolve this map by a modification $V'\to V$. The pulled-back incidence family $G\subset V'\times U$ is irreducible and has fibers of pure dimension $\dim U-\dim V$, by [ Definition 1.5, Theorem 1.6 and Proposition 1.9 , Campana2004 ] , and its evaluation $G\to U$ is bimeromorphic. Resolve $G$ inside the compact Kähler product to obtain $U'$. A divisor of $U'$ whose image in $V'$ has codimension at least two must have image of codimension at least two in $G$: otherwise that image, of dimension $\dim U-1$, would force a fiber dimension greater than $\dim U-\dim V$. It is therefore exceptional over $U$ as well. This constructs the required neat model. Further source modifications preserve this property while the base is fixed. Apply this construction after resolving the leaf quotient, then take its relative maximal rationally connected quotient and resolve its maps. The relative quotient is the cycle-space input [ Theorem 2.7 and Proposition 2.8 , Campana2004 ] ; its specialization identifies the rational quotient of a very general fiber. Its quotient fibers are rationally connected. Their residual bases are not uniruled by the projective section theorem [ Theorem 1.1 , GHS2001 ] and its Kähler reduction [ Lemma 8.10 , Ou2025 ] . In that reduction, a rationally connected fibration over a curve has no holomorphic two-forms: both degree-one and degree-two forms on its general fiber vanish, and the cotangent filtration gives the assertion on the total space. Its smooth Kähler model is then projective by the vanishing-to-projectivity criterion , so the section theorem applies. These quotient and class-C existence results remain explicit external inputs. Apply the neat-model construction once more to the resolved relative quotient, modifying its base $Z$ and keeping $Y$ fixed. We obtain compact Kähler manifolds and holomorphic fibrations \[  \pi :\widehat X\longrightarrow X,\qquad p=s\circ r:\widehat X\xrightarrow {r}Z\xrightarrow {s}Y,  \] where $\pi $ is a modification and every $p$-exceptional or $r$-exceptional divisor is $\pi $-exceptional. Here exceptional for a fibration means that its image has codimension at least two. Let $\widehat{\mathcal F}$ be the induced foliation and $\beta =\pi ^*\alpha $. Its minimum slope is still positive by lemma 9.75.2 . Put $\mathcal H=\ker (ds)$, saturated, and suppose its rank $h$ is positive. The differential defines a holomorphic map $\widehat{\mathcal F}\to r^*T_ Z$. Let $\mathcal J$ be its image and $\overline{\mathcal J}$ its saturation in $r^*T_ Z$. The image has rank $h$ and is a torsion-free quotient of $\widehat{\mathcal F}$. Off a codimension-two subset of $Z$, $\mathcal H\subset T_ Z$ is a subbundle, and on its inverse image $\overline{\mathcal J}=r^*\mathcal H$. Consequently \[  \det \overline{\mathcal J} =r^*\det \mathcal H\otimes \mathcal O_{\widehat X}(E),  \] where $E$ is supported on $r$-exceptional divisors. Neatness and the definition of $\beta $ give $\beta \cdot E=0$. Saturation adds an effective divisor, so \[  \deg _\beta (r^*\det \mathcal H) =\deg _\beta \overline{\mathcal J} \geq \deg _\beta \mathcal J \geq h\mu _{\beta ,\min }(\widehat{\mathcal F})>0.  \] Choose a rational Hodge class on $Z$ by lemma 9.75.1 , say $[a+\tau +\bar\tau ]$. The holomorphic two-form $r^*\tau $ vanishes on $\Lambda ^2\widehat{\mathcal F}$ by lemma 9.75.2 . At generic points the differential maps onto $r^*\mathcal H$, so $\tau |_{\Lambda ^2\mathcal H}=0$. On every smooth $s$-fiber the rational class therefore restricts to the Kähler class of $a$. Every such fiber is projective by the integral projectivity criterion. Let $Y^\circ $ be the nonempty open set where $s$ is smooth; its complement is a proper analytic subset, and $Y^\circ $ is connected. We use independently Fujiki's deformation theorem [ Proposition 2.3 , Fujiki1981 ] : in a proper smooth family with connected fibers over a connected base, locally dominated by a proper Kähler family, one uniruled fiber makes every fiber uniruled. Here $s^{-1}(Y^\circ )$ is Kähler and the identity supplies that domination. The very general residual fiber is not uniruled by the relative MRC input. Hence every fiber over $Y^\circ $ is not uniruled. Projective BDPP, [ Theorem 2.6 , BDPP2012 ] , makes all their canonical bundles pseudo-effective. This is the canonical-bundle uniruledness implication of BDPP, with precisely the open-set fiber hypothesis needed to apply theorem 10.105.2 on $Z$ with $L=0$. It follows that $K_{Z/Y}-D(s)$ is pseudo-effective. The determinant $\det \mathcal H^*$ differs from this class only by $s$-exceptional divisors. At a general divisor mapping onto a divisor of $Y$, local coordinates $t_1=z_1^ m$ give the correction $m-1$ in $D(s)$ after saturating the differential; elsewhere in codimension one the smooth tangent sequence applies, except for the $s$-exceptional divisors. Reflexive determinants are determined by these codimension-one data. The pullback of each $s$-exceptional divisor is supported on $p$-exceptional divisors, hence on $\pi $-exceptional divisors. Pulling back the pseudo-effective class and pairing with $\beta $ therefore gives $\deg _\beta (r^*\det \mathcal H^*)\geq 0$, contradicting the strict positive degree of $r^*\det \mathcal H$. Thus $\mathcal H=0$, and the general fibers of $p$ are rationally connected. The relative-adjoint application uses the smooth Kähler form $a$ on $Z$ itself; no smoothness of a fiber-integrated form is required. $\square$ Corollary 9.75.4 . 745947D9E1A8 If an involutive saturated sheaf $\mathcal E\subset T_ X$ has $\mu _\alpha (\mathcal E)>0$, its first Harder–Narasimhan piece is an algebraic foliation with rationally connected general leaves. In particular $X$ is uniruled and $K_ X$ is not pseudo-effective. Proof. The first piece is involutive by corollary 10.107.2 and its minimum slope equals its positive slope. Apply the theorem. A covering family of rational curves has positive anticanonical degree and nonnegative degree against every pseudo-effective class, as proved below. Thus $K_ X$ cannot be pseudo-effective. $\square$

title: 10.109 Numerical dimension and cotangent quotients

section: 9.76 Tangent slopes and covering rational curves
text: Ambient manifolds are connected unless stated otherwise. Fibers need not be connected; the section-envelope arguments treat their connected components separately. We use uniruledness in the sense of a dominating family of nonconstant rational curves. After shrinking a smooth parameter space $S$, such a family is a holomorphic map $F:\mathbb P^1\times S\to X$. Indeed, for a dominant meromorphic parametrization its codimension-two indeterminacy set has proper analytic image under the proper projection to $S$; remove that image and take a connected parameter open set. Lemma 9.76.1 . 4F2E71913C12 Let $F:\mathbb P^1\times S\to X$ be a dominating holomorphic family of nonconstant maps to a compact Kähler manifold, with $S$ smooth and connected. The common curve class $\alpha =(F|_{\mathbb P^1\times \{ s\} })_*[\mathbb P^1]$ is movable and $-K_ X\cdot \alpha \geq 2$. Proof. The homology class is constant along paths in the connected parameter space. Choose $(z,s)$ where $F$ is a submersion and $df_ z\ne 0$, with $f=F|_{\mathbb P^1\times \{ s\} }$. Differentiating $F$ in any parameter tangent direction gives a global holomorphic section of $f^*T_ X$. The domain tangent direction is also the value of a global section, since global automorphism fields span $T_{\mathbb P^1,z}$. Consequently these sections span $(f^*T_ X)_ z$. If $n=\dim X$, choose $n-1$ such sections whose values are independent modulo the line $df_ z(T_{\mathbb P^1,z})$. Wedging them with the differential defines a nonzero holomorphic map \[  \mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(2)=T_{\mathbb P^1} \longrightarrow \det (f^*T_ X).  \] Its zero divisor is effective, so $-K_ X\cdot \alpha =\deg \det (f^*T_ X)\geq 2$. For any fixed positive closed $(1,1)$-current on $X$, dominance of $F$ makes the pullbacks of its local potentials well-defined: the submersive locus is dense, so none is identically $-\infty $ on a source open set. Fubini then gives a defined positive current on almost every fiber of $\mathbb P^1\times S\to S$. Its integral equals the cohomological degree and is nonnegative. That degree is constant in this family, so the curve class pairs nonnegatively with every pseudo-effective class. The cited cone duality makes it movable. One need not choose the same generic curve separately for an uncountable collection of currents: each degree is already fixed by the common homology class. $\square$ Corollary 9.76.2 . 8876081BAAEC For positive-dimensional compact Kähler $X$, the following are equivalent: $X$ is uniruled; $\mu _{\alpha ,\max }(T_ X)>0$ for some movable $\alpha $; $\mu _\alpha (T_ X)>0$ for some movable $\alpha $. Moreover $X$ is uniruled if and only if $K_ X$ is not pseudo-effective. Proof. The third condition implies the second by definition. The positive first destabilizing piece proves that the second implies the first. The preceding lemma gives, for the first, \[  \mu _\alpha (T_ X)=\frac{-K_ X\cdot \alpha }{n}>0,  \] which proves the third condition with the rank denominator. It also shows uniruledness excludes a pseudo-effective canonical class. Conversely cone duality applied to a non-pseudo-effective canonical class gives a movable class of positive average tangent slope. This is the third condition. $\square$

title: 9.77 Deformation of the canonical pseudo-effective cone
search_title: Deformation of the canonical pseudo-effective cone
section: 9.77 Deformation of the canonical pseudo-effective cone
text: Ambient manifolds are connected unless stated otherwise. Fibers need not be connected; the section-envelope arguments treat their connected components separately. The geometric input here is deformation invariance of uniruledness: in a proper smooth family over a connected base which is locally dominated by a proper Kähler family, one uniruled fiber forces every fiber to be uniruled. In particular it applies to a proper holomorphic submersion with Kähler total space. This is the precise external deformation theorem of Fujiki, [ Proposition 2.3 , Fujiki1981 ] ; a complete proof of the relative cycle-space compactness and uniruled deformation theorem is not inferred merely from openness of free curves. Corollary 9.77.1 . 11B2C808741A Let $p:\mathcal X\to \mathbb D$ be a proper holomorphic submersion with Kähler total space and connected fibers. If $K_{\mathcal X_0}$ is pseudo-effective, then so is $K_{\mathcal X_ t}$ for every $t\in \mathbb D$. Proof. If some fiber had non-pseudo-effective canonical bundle, corollary 9.76.2 would make it uniruled. The stated deformation theorem would make the central fiber uniruled as well. That same corollary would contradict pseudo-effectivity of its canonical bundle. $\square$
